description: the unattended triage control loop exists and is executable — the automation counterpart to the interactive investigator
command: [ -x scripts/triage-run.sh ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: the event-envelope validator exists and is executable — a trigger you cannot trust is a trigger you must not act on
command: [ -x scripts/event-validate.sh ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: ENVELOPE: a well-formed CI event validates and carries a correlation_id — the field the whole reliability contract keys off
command: scripts/event-validate.sh --field correlation_id fixtures/events/ci-incident.json | grep -q '^INC-002-' && echo pass || echo fail

description: ENVELOPE (fail-closed): an event with no correlation_id is rejected at exit 3 — no correlation_id, no run; it can never be safely deduplicated
command: echo '{"id":"x","source":"ci","type":"t","time":"now","subject":"orders-api"}' | scripts/event-validate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: CORRELATION ID: a fresh event is triaged — the loop validates the envelope, collects read-only evidence, and produces one packet
command: scripts/triage-run.sh --reset >/dev/null; scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json --field outcome

description: STRUCTURED RESULT: the triage packet validates against the sre-investigator evidence schema — a sourced hypothesis with out_of_scope, not free prose
command: scripts/triage-run.sh --reset >/dev/null; scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json >/dev/null 2>&1; scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json --field packet 2>/dev/null | bash scripts/evidence-validate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: DEDUPLICATION: the SAME event delivered twice is deduplicated on the second delivery — same event twice must not mean double action
command: scripts/triage-run.sh --reset >/dev/null; scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json >/dev/null 2>&1; scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json --field outcome

description: IDEMPOTENCY: processing the same correlation_id twice leaves EXACTLY ONE packet — the write is keyed by correlation_id, a re-run is a no-op
command: scripts/triage-run.sh --reset >/dev/null; scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json >/dev/null 2>&1; scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json >/dev/null 2>&1; ls agentops/triage-state/packet-*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '

description: CANCELLATION: a cancel token aborts the loop cleanly with outcome cancelled — no partial packet is left behind
command: scripts/triage-run.sh --reset >/dev/null; C=$(mktemp); scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json --cancel-file "$C" --field outcome; rm -f "$C"

description: CANCELLATION: after a cancelled run, zero packets exist — abort means no side effect, not a half-written artifact
command: scripts/triage-run.sh --reset >/dev/null; C=$(mktemp); scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json --cancel-file "$C" >/dev/null 2>&1; rm -f "$C"; ls agentops/triage-state/packet-*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '

description: RETRY BUDGET + TIMEOUT: a probe that never succeeds exhausts a BOUNDED retry budget and gives up as timed-out — never an infinite loop (the INC-002 lesson)
command: scripts/triage-run.sh --reset >/dev/null; printf '{"specversion":"1.0","id":"e","correlation_id":"INC-999-x","source":"ci","type":"t","time":"now","subject":"orders-api","data":{"incident":"INC-999","env":"staging"}}' > /tmp/m17chk-bad.json; scripts/triage-run.sh --event /tmp/m17chk-bad.json --max-retries 2 --field outcome; rm -f /tmp/m17chk-bad.json

description: READ-ONLY SAFETY: when the loop is asked to deploy, it routes the write through the action boundary and refuses — the automation has no path to production
command: scripts/triage-run.sh --reset >/dev/null; scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json --attempt-deploy --field outcome

description: READ-ONLY SAFETY: a refused deploy leaves zero packets — a blocked write does not silently partial-commit evidence either
command: scripts/triage-run.sh --reset >/dev/null; scripts/triage-run.sh --event fixtures/events/ci-incident.json --attempt-deploy >/dev/null 2>&1; ls agentops/triage-state/packet-*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '

description: READ-ONLY SAFETY: the boundary the loop delegates to refuses an irreversible production action (delete) — the last line proving triage cannot remediate
command: scripts/action-boundary-check.sh --env production --action delete --field outcome

description: YOUR RECEIVER: scripts/alert-receiver.js exists — the webhook endpoint Alertmanager has been posting into a void
command: [ -f scripts/alert-receiver.js ] && echo present || echo missing

description: YOUR RECEIVER: it builds the envelope fields the contract requires — correlation_id, source, type, subject
command: [ -f scripts/alert-receiver.js ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; ok=1; for k in correlation_id source type subject; do grep -q "$k" scripts/alert-receiver.js || ok=0; done; [ "$ok" -eq 1 ] && echo complete || echo incomplete

description: CORRELATION ID: derived from alertname + startsAt, not the per-delivery id or fingerprint — a redelivery of the same incident must key the same
command: [ -f scripts/alert-receiver.js ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'alertname' scripts/alert-receiver.js && grep -q 'startsAt' scripts/alert-receiver.js && echo stable || echo unstable

description: THE REPAIR: the Alertmanager webhook no longer points at localhost — inside a container that is the container itself, so the receiver never heard from it
command: [ -f observability/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'localhost:9095' observability/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml && echo unreachable || echo reachable

description: REAL DELIVERY: at least one envelope in agentops/events/ was written by a real Alertmanager POST, and it validates
command: f=$(ls agentops/events/*.json 2>/dev/null | head -1); [ -n "$f" ] || { echo none; exit 0; }; scripts/event-validate.sh --field correlation_id "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo delivered || echo invalid

description: REAL DELIVERY: the envelope came from alertmanager, not from a hand-written fixture
command: f=$(ls agentops/events/*.json 2>/dev/null | head -1); [ -n "$f" ] || { echo none; exit 0; }; [ "$(jq -r .source "$f")" = "alertmanager" ] && echo real || echo synthetic

description: NO FAKE HYPOTHESIS: triage-run.sh invokes a real model with a schema instead of templating the finding with jq
command: [ -f scripts/triage-run.sh ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'unattended read-only triage collected evidence for' scripts/triage-run.sh && echo templated || { grep -q 'json-schema' scripts/triage-run.sh && echo model-call || echo neither; }

description: FAIL CLOSED ON THE MODEL: the model's structured output is extracted and validated before it reaches disk — a packet the model got wrong must never be written
command: [ -f scripts/triage-run.sh ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'structured_output' scripts/triage-run.sh && grep -q 'evidence-validate' scripts/triage-run.sh && echo guarded || echo unguarded

description: SCHEDULED TRIGGER: platform/schedules/ carries a timer or plist that runs the triage scan unattended
command: ls platform/schedules/* >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo present || echo missing
